lines.text: What if two stars could align?
Not touching, just perfectly in line, from one point of view.
The far one is twenty-six thousand light years away.
The near star's gravity bends the far one's light into a ring around it.
Too small for you to see.
But you see it brighten, with light that left before anyone wrote a word.
Einstein worked it out in nineteen thirty six, and said we'd never catch one.
Telescopes now catch thousands every year.
Each lasts a few weeks, and some get a thousand times brighter.
A tiny blip in that glow can even reveal a hidden planet.
The odds for any one star, right now?
One in a million, and it keeps happening.
That's what it means to align.
